body.estimand_functional: \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=\sum_{k=-2r}^{2r}\{\mathbb E_P[Z_0^{(1)}Z_k^{(2)}]-\tau_{\mathrm P}^2\}\), with the mean-centered test \(\phi_{n,\alpha}=\mathbf 1\{\widehat\Omega_n^{12}>t_n(\alpha)\}\); the lag-\((2r+1)\) statistic satisfies \(\mathbb E_P[\widehat\Omega_n^{\mathrm u}]=\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  In the canonical full-observable experiment, whose vector contains the observed graph, both assignments, both exposures, both realized outcomes, and the known propensity coordinates, \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\); the score-vector radius \(s_{n,\alpha,\beta}^{\mathrm{score}}=\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) is a corollary.  Both rates hold for distinct focal labels \(e_1\ne e_0\), fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are applied to the same graph, exposure mapping, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule after a prespecified washout; the covariance cutoff and analysis interior are fixed before assignment.
sampling_model.units: The canonical specialization observes \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzes \(I_n=\{r+1,\ldots,n-r\}\). Outside one law-null set independent of assignment, a joint radius-\(r\) Borel cylinder map represents every exposure--outcome assignment cell. On the buffered interior, the finite exposure, realized-outcome, propensity, and score coordinates are explicitly induced by that same map and the restricted primitive coordinates.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments in each wave generate local exposure labels and realized outcomes under one common shift-equivariant schedule; the left shift satisfies \((\theta^kd)_j=d_{j+k}\) and \(\{i,j\}\in\theta^kG\) if and only if \(\{i+k,j+k\}\in G\). The full minimax observation contains the finite graph, both assignments, both exposure arrays, both realized-outcome arrays, and known propensity coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave, so every IPW division in both the infinite and explicitly restricted finite scores is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Propensities are known from the Bernoulli design and are computed on the buffered interior from the same local exposure cylinder. The mean-centered statistic estimates only the two wave means; the lag-separated statistic removes that centering bias exactly. Neither procedure estimates unit-specific conditional scores or fits a regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 show that zero asymptotic variance for a stationary finite-variance finite-dependent sequence is equivalent to a finite-dependent coboundary and yields an unnormalized endpoint-difference law.
The paper proves consistency and asymptotic normality for exposure-IPW estimators under approximate neighborhood interference and studies network-HAC inference for one randomized finite population.
The paper proves central limit and invariance principles for stationary fields represented as functions of independent innovations under short-range physical dependence.
The paper proves treatment-effect asymptotics under graphon-random interference and develops direct- and indirect-effect inference.

The preprint proves asymptotic normality and optimality for regression-adjusted average-direct-effect estimators under graphon interference and consistently estimates the linear estimator's asymptotic variance under a low-rank graphon condition.

The preprint uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment assignments for average treatment and average spillover effects under network interference.

body.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. A joint assignment--innovation cylinder version, common to every assignment outside one null set, explicitly induces every finite exposure, outcome, propensity, and score coordinate on the buffered interior. Explicit radius-one Rademacher witnesses use the Borel cylinders \(\Psi^{\Delta}(u,x)=(x_0,(u_0-u_{-1})x_0)\) and \(\Psi^+(u,x)=(x_0,u_0x_0)\) with the single null set empty; they show that zero long-run variance can coexist with heterogeneous local scores and that the positive-variance alternative is nonempty. These primitives give order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration, size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic. A verified four-cell local schedule has common support at the level of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, while one-wave interference papers study effect or estimator-variance inference. Viviano2020 develops a two-wave network design in which a pilot estimates variance and the second wave optimizes participation and treatment; these results do not supply a repeated-randomization test of the Palm population-covariance boundary or a full-observation minimax converse for it.
project_justification.niche: Conditional replication removes assignment noise from cross-wave IPW products. The joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition supplies one version simultaneously over all assignment cells, and the buffered restriction uses that same map to induce the finite exposure, outcome, and propensity coordinates. This common local rule yields stationarity and deterministic primitive influence, while four local assignment cells leave unobserved schedule coordinates after two waves and give common support to the induced observed-data laws needed for a full-record information bound.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic under the corrected common local versions. The explicit radius-one cylinders \(\Psi^{\Delta}(u,x)=(x_0,(u_0-u_{-1})x_0)\) and \(\Psi^+(u,x)=(x_0,u_0x_0)\), both valid with the empty exceptional set, certify a heterogeneous zero-variance boundary point and a positive-variance point in the same local class. For distinct focal exposure labels, the project also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_nt^2\) for the complete declared record and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), yielding matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the full observation and its score-vector subexperiment.

body.related_work: Janson2015 supplies the finite-block coboundary result used to interpret the zero boundary, but no two-wave statistic or testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies one-wave exposure-IPW and approximate-neighborhood-interference analysis; no ANI or graph-HAC transfer is used here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known design propensities. Viviano2020 is the closest design comparator: it uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment for average treatment and spillover effects. The present work does not claim that two-wave network designs are new; it uses conditionally independent replications with common joint local versions to identify and test a Palm covariance boundary and proves a full-observation common-support minimax converse. LiWager2022 and FanLengWu2025 target causal-effect estimation and estimator variance under graphon models. Tsybakov2009 supplies the classical Pinsker and two-point testing inequalities used after the new four-cell likelihood calculation.
body.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. The explicit law \(P^{\Delta}\) has \(h_i=U_i-U_{i-1}\), variance \(2\) at each site, lag-one covariances \(-1\), and long-run sum zero; \(P^+\) has \(h_i=U_i\) and long-run variance one. Both laws satisfy the corrected left-shift orientation and the joint radius-one cylinder condition with one empty exceptional set. On the line, the joint cylinder condition makes the conditional score a finite block factor, so Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to one no-carryover schedule and one common joint assignment--innovation cylinder version. The full-observation converse includes the observed finite graph, assignments, exposures, realized outcomes, and known propensities, but not the innovations or unobserved assignment-cell outcomes. The graph extension requires a single bounded local score map shared by all sites and waves, a fixed footprint, and deterministic covariance-support sets on F\o lner interiors. No growing bandwidth, random shortest-path cutoff, approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT or Wald theorem, or BondEtAl2012 reanalysis is claimed.
body.honest_scope: The target is \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), the long-run covariance sum of local conditional exposure-effect scores under the Palm law. The interval results and their finitely generated amenable Cayley-graph extension use a fixed deterministic local cutoff, bounded outcomes, overlap, two conditionally independent waves, common assignment--innovation cylinder versions, bounded primitive influence, and bounded score dependence. The finite interval record is coupled by explicitly inducing its exposure, outcome, propensity, and score coordinates from those same local maps. For distinct focal labels, minimax sharpness holds for the explicitly encoded finite observed-data vector at \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); the score-vector theorem is a corollary. The note claims neither novelty of two-wave designs nor validity for observations revealing innovations or unobserved potential outcomes.
